<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{def:ring}
Fix $N \ge 3$. Index the units by the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}_N = \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$, so
that indices are read modulo $N$ throughout, and let the state space be
$\Omega_N = \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{Z}_N}$. Let $\mathscr{A}_N$ be the substrate on these units whose
transition probability matrix is deterministic and given unit by unit by
\[
  p_z\bigl(s'_z = b \;\big|\; s\bigr) \;=\;
  \begin{cases}
    1, & b = s_z \oplus s_{z+1} \oplus s_{z+2},\\[2pt]
    0, & \text{otherwise,}
  \end{cases}
  \qquad z \in \mathbb{Z}_N,\quad s \in \Omega_N,
\]
where $\oplus$ denotes addition modulo $2$. Equivalently, $\mathscr{A}_N$ is the deterministic
substrate whose global transition map is
\[
  F_N : \Omega_N \to \Omega_N, \qquad
  (F_N s)_z \;=\; s_z \oplus s_{z+1} \oplus s_{z+2}.
\]
The \emph{window} of unit $z$ is $W_z = \{z, z+1, z+2\}$, the set of units it reads. In
the formal development $\mathscr{A}_N$ is \texttt{circNet N}.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:ring-basic}
Let $N \ge 3$ and identify $\Omega_N$ with $\mathbb{F}_2^{\mathbb{Z}_N}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $F_N$ is $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear, with matrix the circulant
  $C = I + P + P^{2}$, where $P$ is the cyclic shift $(Ps)_z = s_{z+1}$.
\item[(ii)] $F_N$ is bijective if and only if $3 \nmid N$.
\item[(iii)] The all-ones state $\mathbf{1} \in \Omega_N$ satisfies $F_N(\mathbf{1}) =
  \mathbf{1}$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
(i) is immediate from the definition, exclusive-or being addition in $\mathbb{F}_2$.
For (ii), circulants form an $\mathbb{F}_2$-algebra isomorphic to
$\mathbb{F}_2[x]/(x^{N}-1)$, the shift $P$ corresponding to $x$; under it $C$ becomes
$f(x) = 1 + x + x^{2}$, and $C$ is invertible exactly when $f$ is a unit, that is when
$\gcd\bigl(f(x),\, x^{N}-1\bigr) = 1$. Since
$f(x) = (x^{3}-1)/(x-1)$, the roots of $f$ are the primitive cube roots of unity, and
these are $N$-th roots of unity precisely when $3 \mid N$. For (iii), each window has
three units, and $1 \oplus 1 \oplus 1 = 1$.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
Informally, $\mathscr{A}_N$ is uniform, sparse and flat: it is invariant under rotation, each
unit reads exactly three units however large $N$ grows, and no unit is distinguished from
any other. In particular it is the opposite of the densely connected architecture one
might expect a large value to require.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:exclusion}
For every $N \ge 8$ with $3 \nmid N$, every background $u$ and \emph{every} state $s$,
the substrate $\mathscr{A}_N$ is a complex:
\[
  \varphi_s(\mathscr{A}_N, s) \;>\; \varphi_s(S', s)
  \qquad \text{for every nonempty proper } S' \subsetneq \mathbb{Z}_N .
\]
More precisely $\varphi_s(\mathscr{A}_N, s) \ge 4$ while $\varphi_s(S', s) < 4$ for every such $S'$.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:lower}
For every $N \ge 8$ with $3 \nmid N$ and every background $u$, the integrated
information of $\mathscr{A}_N$ \emph{at the all-ones state} $\mathbf{1}$ satisfies
\[
  \Phi_{\max}(\mathscr{A}_N, \mathbf{1}) \;\ge\;
  2^{\lfloor N^2/8 \rfloor}\cdot\frac{(1/2)^{N}}{2N} \;-\; 1 .
\]
In particular $\log_2 \Phi_{\max}(\mathscr{A}_N, \mathbf{1}) = \Omega(N^2)$. Unlike
Theorem~\ref{thm:exclusion}, this is a statement about a single state.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:damage}
Let $S = \mathbb{Z}_N$ and let the state be all-ones, with $3 \nmid N$ and $N \ge 4$. Then for
every system partition $\theta$,
\[
  \varphi_s(\theta) \;=\; \mathrm{dmg}(\theta),
\]
and consequently
\[
  \varphi_s(\mathscr{A}_N, \mathbf{1}) \;=\;
  \max\Bigl\{ \mathrm{dmg}(\theta) \;:\;
  \theta \in \operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\vartheta}
  \frac{\mathrm{dmg}(\vartheta)}{\mathcal{N}(\vartheta)} \Bigr\}.
\]
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:competitor}
For every nonempty proper $S \subsetneq \mathbb{Z}_N$ at the all-ones state,
\[
  \varphi_s(S, \mathbf{1}) \;=\; 2^{-\operatorname{corank}(C_S)}\cdot \mathrm{dmgval}(S),
\]
where $\mathrm{dmgval}(S)$ is the maximum of $\mathrm{dmg}$ over the minimizers of
$\mathrm{dmg}/\mathcal{N}$ among partitions of $S$.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:d1}
A partition of $\mathbb{Z}_N$ damaging exactly one unit has $\mathcal{N}(\theta) = N-1$.
\textup{(\texttt{sysCutCount\_eq\_of\_damagedCount\_one})}
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:d2}
A partition of $\mathbb{Z}_N$ damaging exactly two units has either
$\mathcal{N}(\theta) = 2(N-1)$, the case of two singleton inputs blocks, or
$4\,\mathcal{N}(\theta) \le N^{2}$, the case of one inputs block and its complement.
\textup{(\texttt{sysCutCount\_of\_damagedCount\_two})}
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:d3}
For $N \ge 8$, a partition of $\mathbb{Z}_N$ damaging exactly three units satisfies
$4\,\mathcal{N}(\theta) \le (N-1)^2 + 8(N-1)$.
\textup{(\texttt{sysCutCount\_of\_damagedCount\_three'})}
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lem:shield}
For $N \ge 3$, $d \notin S$ with $d-1 \in S$, and $1 \le T \le N-2$ with $P$ and
$S \setminus P$ both nonempty, the partition above damages exactly one unit of $S$.
\textup{(\texttt{damagedCountOn\_shield})}
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:crude}
For every proper $S \subsetneq \mathbb{Z}_N$ with $|S| \ge 2$, every background and every state
$s$, $\varphi_s(S,s) < 4$. \textup{(\texttt{sysPhi\_circNet\_lt\_four})}
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:arcsare}
Let $N \ge 3$ with $3 \nmid N$ and let the state be all-ones. Every arc of length
$L \ge 3$ is a distinction of $\mathscr{A}_N$, the arc saturating to the whole cycle once
$L \ge N$. Moreover its maximally irreducible cause purview contains the arc itself, so
that the support of the distinction contains every unit of $M$ in its stated state.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:onlyarcs}
The distinctions of $\mathscr{A}_N$ at the all-ones state are exactly the arcs of length
between $3$ and $N-1$ together with the whole cycle; there are $N(N-3)+1$ of them.
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
\label{rem:status}
Proposition~\ref{prop:onlyarcs} is the one statement in this paper that is \emph{not}
part of the formal development. It is established by exhaustive evaluation over all
$2^N$ mechanisms for $N = 8, 10, 11, 13$, cross-checked against an independent exact
implementation, with the counts $41, 71, 89, 131$ agreeing with $N(N-3)+1$ and with no
non-arc distinction and no arc of length one or two appearing. The argument for general
$N$ is the criterion used in that evaluation---the effect information of $M$ is positive
if and only if some connected component of $D(M)$ in the window-overlap graph has window
union equal to $M$, and the cause information is positive if and only if $M$ is connected
in that graph---from which the classification follows; formalizing it is routine but was
not carried out. Nothing in Theorems~\ref{thm:exclusion} or~\ref{thm:lower} depends on
it. Its role here is to show that the quadratic rate is forced: a family of $2^{cN}$
distinctions sharing a unit would give $\Phi = 2^{2^{\Theta(N)}}$, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:onlyarcs} says no such family exists on this cycle.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{lem:family}
Let $F$ be a family of distinctions of a substrate, all containing a common \emph{stated
unit} $p$, that is a pair (unit, state), in their supports, each satisfying $\varphi_d(d)/|\mathrm{supp}(d)| \ge c > 0$. Then
\[
  \Phi_{\max} \;\ge\; \bigl(2^{|F|} - 1 - |F|\bigr)\,c .
\]
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Fix the unit $0$ and index arcs through it by a pair $(s,e)$ with
$1 \le s < \lfloor N/2 \rfloor$ and $1 \le e < N - \lfloor N/2 \rfloor$, letting
$F$ consist of the arcs running from $-s$ to $e$. Each contains $0$ and has length
$s + e + 1 \ge 3$, so by Proposition~\ref{prop:arcsare} each is a distinction whose
support contains the stated unit $(0, \mathrm{true})$. Distinct pairs give distinct arcs,
so
\[
  |F| \;=\; \bigl(\lfloor N/2 \rfloor - 1\bigr)
            \bigl(N - \lfloor N/2 \rfloor - 1\bigr) \;\ge\; N^{2}/8 .
\]
The support of each contains at most $2N$ stated
units and
$\varphi_d \ge (1/2)^{N}$ by the cause-side estimate of Proposition~\ref{prop:arcsare}, so
$c = (1/2)^N/(2N)$ is a uniform floor. Lemma~\ref{lem:family} gives
\[
  \Phi_{\max} \;\ge\; \bigl(2^{|F|} - 1 - |F|\bigr)\cdot\frac{(1/2)^N}{2N}
  \;\ge\; 2^{\lfloor N^2/8\rfloor}\cdot\frac{(1/2)^N}{2N} - 1 . \qedhere
\]
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
\label{rem:constants}
Both constants are generous. The true family has $\sum_{L=3}^{N-1}\min(L+2,N)+1 \approx
N^2/2$ members, measured as $35, 56, 68, 95$ at $N = 8, 10, 11, 13$. The true floor is
not $2^{-N}/(2N)$ but approximately $1/(2N)$: the support of an arc of length $L$ has
$\min(L+2,N)$ units, and $\varphi_d$ equals $1/4$ for $L = 3$, $1/2$ for
$4 \le L \le N-2$, $3/2$ for $L = N-1$ and $4$ for the whole cycle. Substituting these
gives a bound of the form $2^{N^2/2}/(2N)$, non-vacuous from small $N$ on. We proved the
crude version because it suffices for the growth rate and because the sharp values
require the exact purview computation of Proposition~\ref{prop:onlyarcs}, which is not
formalized.
<!-- end remark-3 -->
